title: One Live Northbeam Renew Trade-In Agreement per Serial
content:
**Clause.** A customer may hold as many Northbeam Renew Trade-In agreements as they have devices to trade, and the number on one profile is not limited in itself. A second agreement is never opened on a serial that already carries one standing in quoted, accepted, device received or appraised. A batch agreement covers up to its programme's device count on one record, and each serial inside the batch still counts once toward the profile's yearly figures. Where a quote has expired or the device has been sent back, a fresh quote may be written on the same serial, and the earlier agreement stays on file.

**How the duplicate is judged.** The bar rests on the retailer's own trade-in agreement records and not on what the customer says about earlier trades, and it is judged before the new quote is written. The records are matched by the serial or IMEI of the device: an agreement already standing on that serial in quoted, accepted, device received or appraised is the one that bars a second. Two agreements on the same serial are separate records told apart by the day each quote was given and the Renew programme each was written under, so an expired or returned agreement stays on file beside the fresh one rather than being overwritten.

**Where the bar does and does not bite.**

| Records on the serial | A fresh quote on that serial |
| --- | --- |
| an agreement standing quoted | barred |
| an agreement standing accepted | barred |
| an agreement standing device received | barred |
| an agreement standing appraised | barred |
| an agreement standing expired | open |
| an agreement standing returned to the customer | open |

**Batch agreements.** One batch record may cover up to the device count its Renew programme allows, so a business profile trading a pallet does not need one agreement per machine. That concession is about how many records are kept, not about the yearly figures: every serial inside the batch counts once toward the profile's yearly figures.
